title: Condition inverted for TYPE_CHECKING block
detail: The block is executed only during type checking, hiding __getattr__ from runtime and causing AttributeError for __version__.
note: Says the condition is inverted: `__getattr__` exists only for type checkers, so `__version__` fails at runtime.

title: __getattr__ defined only during type checking
detail: The function should be defined at module level so it is available at runtime.
note: The planted negation again: `__getattr__` is defined only for type checkers.

title: Incorrect package name in version lookup
detail: The __getattr__ implementation returns the version of the 'werkzeug' package instead of 'jinja2', causing incorrect version reporting and potential AttributeError if Werkzeug is not installed.
note: Real: the merged PR looks up the version of `werkzeug`, not `jinja2`. Its maintainers fixed it two minutes after it merged.

title: Condition inverted in __getattr__
detail: The code triggers deprecation logic for any attribute other than __version__, which is the opposite of the intended behavior. This causes normal attribute access to raise AttributeError and misleads users.
note: Says the condition is inverted: every attribute but `__version__` takes the deprecation path.

title: AttributeError on non-Failure response
detail: When the response is not a twisted Failure, the code accesses response.flags without checking that the attribute exists. If response is a plain Response object, this raises AttributeError, breaking the timeout handling.

title: Incorrect logical operator in cancellation handling
detail: The code triggers the dataloss flag when the stream is cancelled or when a partial body should be kept, but it should only trigger when both conditions are true. Using 'or' causes the flag to be set even when the stream is not cancelled, leading to incorrect response handling.
note: Describes the planted `or` and says it should need both.

title: Incorrect raw mode detection
detail: Any short option containing the letter 'r' (e.g., '-r', '-rx') causes the function to return False, disabling raw mode even when the option is actually requesting raw control characters. This misclassifies valid raw mode requests and can break color support.
note: Describes the planted `return False`: a short flag with an `r` in it isn't detected.

title: Blocking subprocess call without timeout
detail: The temporary file pager uses subprocess.call to invoke the pager program. If the pager hangs or takes too long, the entire process blocks indefinitely because no timeout is specified and the call is not wrapped in a try/except that would handle KeyboardInterrupt or other signals.
note: A pager runs until the user quits it, so a timeout would cut it off; nothing is wrong.
